topic: Impact of Electronics on Everyday Life
title: Electronics in Your Home Explained Simply | PUC Electronics Class 11
description:
Diya has a fever, and a digital thermometer reads 38.1 degrees in seconds. How does a tiny stick do that? In this animated lesson we open it up: a thermistor whose resistance falls as it warms, a converter that turns a voltage into numbers, a microcontroller and a display, all changing live together. Then we walk through a home and spot the electronic blocks in a phone charger (230 V AC in, about 5 V DC out), a washing machine and a fridge.

On a live breadboard a TV remote sends its code as flashes of invisible infrared light, and the oscilloscope shows the pattern sent and the pattern the TV receives. We show why a battery's milliampere hours are a charge (current times time), work out that a 4000 mAh battery at 250 mA lasts 16 hours, and weigh the impact of electronics: video calls, digital payments, online learning and patient monitors on one side, e-waste, screen time and online fraud on the other. Then the exam trap (mAh is charge, not current; 1 mAh = 3.6 C), where it is asked, an original JEE Main pattern practice question with a full solution, and a formula card to screenshot.

This is Episode 5 of PUC Electronics, Class 11, Chapter 1: Introduction to Electronics (Karnataka PUC Electronics).
